title: Author-labelled answers for the eighteen M1 duel items (1774 Coercive-Acts slate)
whyThisExists: The build plan requires the grading service to ship behind an eval set stocked with correct-but-unusually-worded answers, because a false negative costs a student a gunfight they earned. The rubrics in duel-items.json already carry accept and reject examples, and a classifier that only reproduces those has been tested on its own answer key. Every answer in this file is deliberately absent from the rubric it tests, so passing it means the rubric generalised.

calibratedAgainst.why: Twelve real Texas eighth-grade responses to a real released STAAR short constructed response on 8.4(A) — the exact standard all three M1 concepts sit under — each carrying the score a trained TEA scorer gave and that scorer's written reason. The rules below are read off it rather than invented.
rulesRead: Naming an issue and explaining nothing scores zero, even when two issues are named correctly.
Vague affect scores zero however long and fluent the answer is.
The substantive core in a student's own rough words scores full credit at eleven words with two misspellings.
Incidental slips are not the disqualifier: TEA credited a response dated 'Proclamation of 1863' and a full-mark response that blamed 'The British Monarchy'.
calibratedAgainst.readOnly: content/staar belongs to another pass. Nothing here modifies it.

howToRun.input: gradingPolicy from duel-items.json, plus the one item's question, referenceAnswer and rubric, plus the answer string.
howToRun.report: false-negative rate separately from false-positive rate, never as one accuracy number.
howToRun.gate: Zero false negatives on the CORRECT rows is the shipping condition. False positives on the WRONG rows are a tuning target, not a blocker.
howToRun.sampleSize: 75 rows across 18 items is a smoke test that catches a grader scoring style, spelling or keyword overlap. It is not enough to certify one, and it contains no responses from real students; that gap can only be closed by playtest transcripts. The three REP two-part items carry rows that give only one half, labelled WRONG with the missing half named.
